This petition under Section 439 Cr.P.C. with the following prayer:
 "WHEREFORE, the petitioner most  respectively pray that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to release him on bail for the offence under Sections 498A, 307, 54 of IPC in Crime No.7/2023 of Kushal Nagar Town Police Station, Kodagu District, on the file of Civil Judge and JMFC, Kushalnagar in the interest of justice."

sentences.text:
3. The brief facts of the case are as under:
Sri.Shashikala R lodged a complaint with Kushalnagar Town Police Station on 14.01.2023, which was registered in Crime No.7/2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 307 and 504 of IPC 4.
The gist of the complaint averments reveal that the complainant is working as a Head Constable in Kushalanagar Town Police Station and is residing in the police quarters.

About 11 years earlier,
she has married K.G.Nagendra and there are two children's in the marriage aged 9 years and 3 years respectively.
It is her contention that her husband is a drunkard and he had borrowed money from all possible sources and has become a defaulter.

A sum of Rs.13,00,000/- is borrowed by her husband as a loan from different people and in that regard, there was serious differences between the complainant and accused in their matrimonial relationship.

There was annual sports meet between 14.11.2022 to 19.11.2022 at Madikeri and complainant and her friends had participated in the annual sports meet and they had commuted from Kushalnagar to Madikeri in a car of one of her colleagues by name Sandeep by sharing petrol charges.
In that regard, accused - petitioner had entertained doubt as to the fidelity of the complainant and picked up a quarrel.
5. In the quarrel, the accused had assaulted the complainant with helmet on her head resulting in injury.
6. Based on the complaint, the police registered the case as aforesaid and investigated the matter and inter alia arrested the petitioner and took him to custody and then, filed the charge sheet.

sentences.text: 7. The charge sheet materials reveal that the complainant has sustained simple injuries.
8. The attempt made by the petitioner seeking grant of bail is rejected by the learned District Judge in Crl.Misc.No.53/2023 by order dated 23.02.2023.
Thereafter, the petitioner is before this Court.

9. Sri.Lathif B, learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently contended that even assuming that the entire materials on record is to be accepted as true for the purpose of arguments, no ingredients whatsoever are made out to attract the offence punishable under Section 307 of IPC and therefore,
sought for grant of bail.

10. He also pointed out that since charge sheet is filed and the petitioner is a Teacher and he is having permanent residence, continuation of the accused - petitioner in judicial custody is no longer warranted and sought for grant of bail.
11. Per contra, the learned HCGP opposes the bail petition by reiterating the ground urged in the objection statement.

He also pointed out that the petitioner had the habit of attacking the complainant for silly reasons and the same was tolerated by the complainant all these years only with an intention to maintaining the matrimonial relationship for the sake of the children and when the petitioner has gone to the extent of assaulting the complainant on her head with helmet with an intention to take away her life, she could no longer tolerate the same and therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for grant of bail.
12.
In view of rival contention of the parties, this Court perused the materials on record meticulously.

On such perusal of the materials on record, it is seen that the incident has occurred on an unfortunate day when the complainant had participated in the annual sports meet and for that purpose, she had traveled in the car of the colleague of the complainant.
The accused - petitioner doubted her chastity and picked up quarrel.
In the spur of the movement, he had taken the helmet and assaulted the complainant on her head.
13. Whether at all the petitioner had an intention to murder the complainant or not, cannot be decided by this Court at this stage.
It is for the learned trial Judge to form an opinion as to the alleged guilt of the petitioner after the full fledged trial based on the materials available on record.

It is too premature for this Court to assess the merits or demerits of the case at this Stage by holding a mini trial as the same may prejudice the case of the parties during trial one way or the other.

14. Suffice to say that since the charge sheet is filed and in absence of any previous complaint, this Court is of the considered opinion that the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail by resorting special power under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
The apprehensions expressed by the prosecution can be meted out by imposing suitable and stringent conditions.

15. Accordingly, the following;
ORDER
The criminal petition is allowed.

The petitioner is directed to be enlarged on bail by the Civil Judge and JMFC, Kushalnagar, in Crime No.7/2023 registered by the Kushal Nagar Town Nagendra K.G vs The State Of Karnataka on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150951793/
3 Police Station, Kodagu, for offence punishable under Sections 498A, 307 and 54 of IPC on following conditions:
(i) The petitioner shall execute a bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Only) with two sureties for the like sum to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge;
(ii) The petitioner shall make a separate residence till the conclusion of the Trial.
